private_notes.private_reasoning: I’m opening with a substantial but supportable demand, reflecting the sizable disputed charges, the merits risk to both sides, and the value of automatic distribution to an identifiable class. I’m seeking fees in addition to the class fund and terms that protect class members if the court reduces the fee award.

Their $52 million demand exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Make a credible but firm counter that preserves automatic distribution while reducing both the class fund and fee request. Keep the total outlay well below the ceiling, reject clear sailing, and have any unawarded fee revert to Brightline.

Counter within Brightline’s stated all-in limit while seeking stronger protections for the class and a fee arrangement that compensates counsel for the substantial work and expenses invested. Preserve automatic distribution.

The latest proposal totals $30 million, within Brightline’s $40 million authorization, and provides automatic payments to the identifiable class. Accepting resolves the litigation on the available terms; the fee provisions do not increase Brightline’s agreed cash outlay.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the settlement through arm’s-length negotiations. Consistent with the confidentiality of the mediation, this statement does not disclose mediation communications or negotiation positions. The settlement provides a $24 million class fund, automatic distribution to identified class members, and a separate fee-and-expense payment subject to court approval. The parties also agreed that any portion of the requested fee not awarded by the Court will benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline.
